name: Highland Park moving vehicle assembly
description: Ford’s Highland Park factory organized workers at stations along moving lines to assemble vehicle components and chassis.

impact.note: Moving-line assembly spread from this factory to industry worldwide, so most people now live with its products; manufacturing was reorganised and mass production grew.

date.label: by 1914
date.basis: The Henry Ford catalogue reports a complete vehicle assembly labour-time comparison by 1914.

events.statement: The museum reports a Model T assembly labour time of just over 1.5 labour-hours by 1914, compared with 12.5 labour-hours under stationary methods.

evidence.supports: The catalogue states the two labour-time figures and dates the comparison by 1914.

events.caveats: Museum summary; boundaries of assembly, components and prior baseline need original production records.

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated case currently researched, not a claim of the capability’s original invention or global priority.

caveats: Moving work began in other industries and Ford stages earlier; the evidence does not establish worldwide invention of an assembly line.

research.note: Independent review checked The Henry Ford’s account and photograph catalogue. The 1914 catalogue comparison is a museum summary; task boundaries and the date of its stationary comparator are not specified.
